6	// Flat, ordered list of every file in the tree (a group's own files, then
7	// its subgroups' files, recursively). Shared by the upload worker (order to
8	// process files in), the upload modal's per-group rollup counts, and the
9	// "every file in this group is done" check driving the Open-in-Drive link —
10	// one traversal so they can't drift out of sync on how they handle nesting.
11	export function flattenFiles(group: LocalFileGroup): LocalFile[] {
12	  return [...group.files, ...group.subgroups.flatMap(flattenFiles)]
13	}

15	// Assigns every group's lookup key in one pass, right after a scan, so no
16	// consumer needs its own tree walk to rebuild it. `key` mirrors the tree's
17	// own nesting (parent key + '/' + name), rooted at null for the scan root.
18	// `group` is the shape ScanLocalRoot actually returns, before `key` exists.
19	function withKeys(group: filetree.LocalFileGroup, key: string | null): LocalFileGroup {
20	  return {
21	    ...group,
22	    key,
23	    subgroups: group.subgroups.map(sub => withKeys(sub, key === null ? sub.name : `${key}/${sub.name}`)),
24	  }

31	  error: string | null
32	  // Resolves to whether a folder was actually picked (false if the user
33	  // cancelled the dialog), so callers know when a fresh root replaced the
34	  // previous one and any per-root state (e.g. the upload queue) should reset.

39	// resulting file/subgroup tree, and loading/error state while ScanLocalRoot
40	// runs. The scan is an async Go RPC that can fail (bad permissions, folder
41	// moved/deleted mid-pick, etc.), so this state needs to live outside the
42	// tree itself — callers can show a spinner or an error message instead of
43	// rendering a stale or partial tree while a scan is in flight.
44	export function useFileTree(): FileTreeHandle {
45	  const [root, setRoot] = useState<string | null>(null)
46	  const [tree, setTree] = useState<LocalFileGroup | null>(null)
47	  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
48	  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
49	
50	  const pickRoot = useCallback(async () => {
51	    const folder = await PickFolder('Choose Root Folder')
52	    if (!folder) return false
53

55	    setLoading(true)
56	    setError(null)

59	    } catch (e) {
60	      setTree(null)
61	      setError(String(e))
62	    } finally {
63	      setLoading(false)
64	    }
65	    return true
66	  }, [])

29	  const readyToUpload = selectedFiles.length > 0 && selectedFiles.every(f => effectiveAssignments!.get(f.path) != null)

content.text:
Because those two buttons are two different DOM elements for the *same* logical action, both visible at once (the toolbar's "Open PDF" is always rendered; the empty-state's "Open PDF" also renders whenever `pdfPath` is null — so they're on screen together whenever there's nothing open yet).

`AsyncButton` instantiates its own `useAsyncAction` internally, so if I'd used it for both buttons, each would get an independent `pending` state — clicking the toolbar button wouldn't stop someone from also clicking the empty-state button, letting two `handleOpen` calls race (two native file dialogs, two `PageCount` calls, etc.).

Calling `useAsyncAction` once at the `SplitMode` component level and wiring the resulting `openAction.pending`/`openAction.run` into both `<Button>`s gives them one shared guard — clicking either disables both until it settles. That's the one case here where the guard needs to be shared across multiple elements rather than scoped to a single button, so it couldn't go through `AsyncButton`.

Staged. `.claude/settings.json` (pre-existing, unrelated to this work) is left out. Here's the drafted commit message — copy it into git gui's message box:

```
Guard async-triggering buttons against repeat clicks while in flight

Adds lib/useAsyncAction.ts, a hook that wraps an async handler with a
re-entrancy guard (a second call is ignored until the first settles)
and routes failures through the shared handleUnexpectedError path, plus
components/AsyncButton.tsx, a thin Button wrapper built on it for the
common case (disables + shows a spinner while pending).

Applies the guard everywhere a button fires an async RPC without one:
MergeMode's Merge & Save, Choose… (File A/B), and Open in Default App;
SplitMode's Export, both Open PDF buttons (sharing one guard via a
component-level useAsyncAction, since they can both be on screen at
once), Output folder…, Open in Finder, and the per-row output-folder
override in OutputFileHeader (ClippedPath gains a disabled prop for
this); DriveUploadMode's Choose root folder…, the per-file "open Drive
folder" icon in UploadModal, and the locked-state Drive-folder badge in
DriveAssignmentField (shared by GroupNode/FileList). Also replaces the
ad hoc try/catch/finally in MergeMode's handleMerge and SplitMode's
handleOpen/handleExport with the hook, removing the now-redundant
merging/exporting state.

DriveFolderPickerModal's per-node expand toggle gets a narrower fix —
disabled while its own ListDriveFolder call is in flight — since it
already had feature-specific inline error handling worth keeping.
Buttons that were already correctly guarded (Upload All, per-file
Retry, Cancel/Resume) are untouched.

Checks off the corresponding item in checklist.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HjiYkj1wT4eCn3H4NCiXaS
```
